column1: # CodeBrix.LilyPort ratchet -- every time a floor came DOWN, and why.
# Append-only, written by `ratchet.py rebaseline`. The manifest records
# what the floor IS; this records what happened to it, so a row that
# reads lower than a plan document claims can always be accounted for.

column5: reason

GENUINE regression from EPG17's first slice, kept deliberately: registering the grace iterator constructor lets \grace be iterated for real, so the file now reaches the unported ly:spanner-broken-into (EPG15's break-substitution.cc). Its page existed only because the grace music was never iterated. Jeremy's ruling 2026-08-07: record the row coming down with the reason rather than reverting the port; the row returns when EPG15 lands.

PHANTOM floor, re-baselined 1541 -> 1444. BatchDriver never cleaned candidate/svg, so each of these rows was graded against a page an EARLIER run had produced, after the file itself had stopped producing one; the ratchet then reported no regression for the failure it exists to catch. First measurement against a clean directory 2026-08-07. Attribution is from the saved sweep logs, which record what each sweep PRODUCED and so do not depend on the directory: 23 stopped at LS-FIX2, 14 at Wave A, 59 at EPG22, and NONE was still producing in the most recent sweep. 78 of the stale pages held zero music glyphs. Causes now: 40 pre-existing parse errors, 29 ly:stencil-extent, 18 no-current-parser (a live defect this exposed), 10 other. Per-row evidence: ~/ClaudeHome/ANALYSIS_lilyport_harnessfix_phantom_rows_2026-08-07.tsv. The engine did not get worse; the measurement was wrong.

Specifically the X-extent default: staff-highlight::height now reads `elements' before it is populated and dies on ly:grob-array->list of (). The fix is not optional - without it every NoteHead answers an EMPTY horizontal extent, which is what killed 23 files when ties first asked for one. EPG22's pattern: these pages stopped being EMPTY and now reach real engraving, where they hit a gap that was always there. Expected to resolve with EPG15/EPG16 line breaking.

RATCHET-FIX ruling, EPG19 session 2026-08-08, Jeremy's GO (option c). REATTRIBUTED TO EPG15/EPG16 and it CANNOT be guarded. The failing beams' stems sit at TWO x-coordinates, 1.2392 and 0.065, running BACKWARDS because the columns are still unplaced; that inverts the segment intervals, an inverted interval is is_empty(), and Beam::calc_x_positions therefore takes its OWN 'beams without segments' fallback. The port's calc_x_positions is upstream's line for line INCLUDING that fallback, so there is nothing here to fix. Fourth instance of the recorded unplaced-columns pattern (EPG10, EPG12, EPG17); the first three were C++ and could be guarded at upstream's own threshold, but this arithmetic is in scm/output-lib.scm, vendored byte-identical, so guarding it would mean editing vendored upstream Scheme. It regressed at EPG14 because EPG14's value_type_check fix stopped discarding the file's own \override Beam.stencil - VERIFIED by removing the override and getting a page back. Not the port drawing anything WRONG: the file reaches real beam formatting for the first time and meets a gap that was always there. The row returns when EPG15/EPG16 place the columns.

RATCHET-FIX ruling, EPG19 session 2026-08-08, Jeremy's GO (option c). OWNED BY EPG16, and a DIFFERENT cause from slashed-beam, which is why it is recorded separately. The file's toplevel expression is a \markup \score-lines block, not a score, and D20's score-level short-circuit in BatchRunner skips toplevel non-score entries BY NAME - the runner says so in its own diagnostic. It produced a page at EPG14 only because the \language leak (RATCHET-FIX finding 7, midi-key-signature.ly including arabic.ly at index 1155) kept the markup from parsing at all; fixing that leak is what exposed this known, recorded limit. Not the port drawing anything WRONG - a documented short-circuit meeting the case it was always going to meet. Closes when EPG16 moves the runner onto the real ly:book-process path.
